A: Consistent file names help you find documents, recognize their contents, and choose the right version without opening every file. They also make handoffs easier because coworkers can follow the same pattern. For example, use `2026-10-24_Acme_Proposal_v02.docx`: the date, client, document type, and version are all visible. Starting with a year-month-day date keeps files in chronological order when sorted by name. Follow your team's naming convention, use the same terms each time, and update the version when you revise a document. Avoid names like `final_final_new.docx`, which leave coworkers guessing about which file to use.
B: Consistent file names help you find the right document quickly and make it easier for coworkers to understand what a file contains without opening it. A shared pattern also helps distinguish projects, dates, and versions, reducing the chance of using an outdated copy. For example, use “2026-10-24_Acme_Meeting-Notes_v01.docx” instead of “notes-final-new.docx.” Putting the date first in year-month-day order keeps files sorted chronologically. Agree on a simple naming pattern with your team, use clear project names, and update version numbers consistently. Keep names descriptive enough to recognize at a glance without making them unnecessarily long.
